metadata.name: Fascism (Italian doctrine, 1927–1932)
metadata.description: Italian Fascism as articulated around 1932: an authoritarian national state, corporatist economic coordination and expansionist politics. Historical description, not endorsement.
metadata.scope: Gentile’s earlier educational foundations, the 1932 Mussolini/Gentile doctrine, 1927 Labour Charter and 1929 Lateran settlement, checked against historical scholarship. This specific Italian variant is not a generic label for present governments. Later 1938 racial legislation is outside scope; Nazi biological claims are not imported.  Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile.
metadata.phrase: An authoritarian national state that subordinates individual and class interests to national unity, corporatist coordination and expansion.

review.notes: Independent revision-2 review against all 240 exact questions, retained numeric claims and unresolved rows. Corrected institutional-premise substitutions and evidence overreach; source-supported nulls remain unresolved. This is a reviewed research draft, not approval to publish an incomplete placement. Question-level findings recorded in the audit report. 1 question corrections. Subsequent restored answers require fresh independent review; earlier peer review does not cover them. Restoration continuation: all 240 records compared with current wording and preceding independent review; 2 new research answers checked against primary passages. Gentile explicitly reverses temperament/character priority in chapter IX, within his actualist educational theory. Disciplined spirit and learnt restraint support qualified self-control inference. These are historical philosophical beliefs, not validated psychology; the earlier educational foundation is disclosed in scope. Incomplete evidence prevents publication; this review does not certify a complete profile.
